purpose: The AES block cipher beneath AES key wrapping (A128KW, A192KW, A256KW), AES-CBC content encryption (A128CBC-HS256, A192CBC-HS384, A256CBC-HS512) and AES-GCM.

audit.note: No public independent audit found. It is widely deployed.

purpose: AES-GCM content encryption (A128GCM, A192GCM, A256GCM) and AES-GCM key wrapping (A128GCMKW, A192GCMKW, A256GCMKW).

audit.note: Reviewed by NCC Group in 2020, for MobileCoin, with no significant findings. The review covered the 0.8 line; polyjose uses a later release line.

purpose: AES key wrapping for A128KW, A192KW and A256KW, also used by ECDH-ES+A128KW, ECDH-ES+A192KW, ECDH-ES+A256KW and the PBES2 algorithms.

audit.note: No public independent audit found. It is widely deployed.

purpose: The CBC mode of AES-CBC content encryption with HMAC (A128CBC-HS256, A192CBC-HS384, A256CBC-HS512).

audit.note: No public independent audit found. It is widely deployed.

purpose: HMAC for HS256, HS384 and HS512 signatures, for the authentication tag of A128CBC-HS256, A192CBC-HS384 and A256CBC-HS512, and inside PBKDF2 for the PBES2 algorithms.

audit.note: No public independent audit found. It is widely deployed.

purpose: SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 for the HS, RS, PS and ES signature algorithms, RSA-OAEP-256, the ECDH-ES key derivation and JWK thumbprints.

audit.note: No public independent audit found. It is widely deployed.

purpose: PBKDF2 key derivation for password-based encryption (PBES2-HS256+A128KW, PBES2-HS384+A192KW, PBES2-HS512+A256KW).

audit.note: No public independent audit found. It is widely deployed.

purpose: The P-256 curve for ES256 signatures and ECDH-ES key agreement.

purpose: The P-384 curve for ES384 signatures and ECDH-ES key agreement.

audit.note: No public independent audit found. It is widely deployed.

purpose: The P-521 curve for ES512 signatures and ECDH-ES key agreement.

audit.note: No public independent audit found. It is widely deployed.

purpose: The secp256k1 curve for ES256K signatures.

audit.note: Reviewed by NCC Group in 2023, for Entropy: two high-severity findings, both fixed. The review covered commits 0f27814 and 5c829a4 of k256 (report page 2, section 1, Executive Summary, Scope), on the 0.13 line; polyjose uses a later release line.

purpose: The ECDSA signature algorithm shared by ES256, ES384, ES512 and ES256K.

audit.note: No public independent audit found. It is widely deployed.

purpose: The elliptic-curve arithmetic, key types and Diffie-Hellman shared by the P-256, P-384, P-521 and secp256k1 curves, for ES256, ES384, ES512, ES256K and ECDH-ES.

audit.note: No public independent audit found. It is widely deployed.

purpose: RSA public-key operations only: verifying RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384 and PS512 signatures and encrypting to RSA-OAEP-256 recipients.

audit.note: Reviewed by Include Security in 2019, with one minor finding. That review predates RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (the Marvin timing attack), and the crate's current rewrite has no published audit. polyjose uses it for public-key operations only.

purpose: The big-integer arithmetic beneath the rsa crate and the elliptic curves, for RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, RSA-OAEP-256, ES256, ES384, ES512, ES256K and ECDH-ES.

audit.note: Reviewed by NCC Group in 2023, for Entropy, in the same review as k256. The review covered commits fde0661 and ad08a7e of crypto-bigint (report page 2, section 1, Executive Summary, Scope), on the 0.5 line; polyjose uses a later release line. The crate's maintainers report no significant findings, and note that the implementation has diverged significantly since that review.

purpose: Clearing private keys, symmetric keys and passwords from memory when they are dropped, for HS256, HS384, HS512, ES256, ES384, ES512, ES256K, EdDSA, ECDH-ES, the AES key-wrap and content-encryption algorithms, dir and PBES2.

audit.note: No public independent audit found. It is widely deployed.

purpose: The Curve25519 arithmetic beneath Ed25519 signatures (EdDSA, Ed25519) and X25519 key agreement (ECDH-ES).

audit.note: Reviewed by Quarkslab in 2019, for Tari, which found minor issues only; x25519-dalek and ed25519-dalek were reviewed only marginally. Fixes came after that review: RUSTSEC-2022-0093 in the 1.x line of ed25519-dalek, and a timing fix in Scalar arithmetic (RUSTSEC-2024-0344). polyjose uses a later release line.

purpose: Ed25519 signatures for the EdDSA and Ed25519 algorithms.

audit.note: No public independent audit found for this crate on its own: Quarkslab's 2019 review of the dalek libraries reviewed it only marginally, and RUSTSEC-2022-0093, which affected its 1.x line, was fixed after that review. It is widely deployed.

purpose: X25519 key agreement for ECDH-ES and ECDH-ES+A128KW, ECDH-ES+A192KW and ECDH-ES+A256KW with X25519 keys.

audit.note: No public independent audit found for this crate on its own: Quarkslab's 2019 review of the dalek libraries reviewed it only marginally. It is widely deployed.

purpose: Comparing and selecting secret values inside the primitives and in polyjose, for example when checking HS256, HS384 and HS512 signatures and AES-CBC-HMAC authentication tags.

audit.note: Reviewed by Quarkslab in 2019, for Tari, as part of its review of the dalek libraries, which found minor issues only. For this crate, the review checked that the source code, and the assembly that the Rust compiler version nightly-2019-06-11 generated from it, have no trivial time leak. In the post's words, the review "does not validate that the library is immune to time leaks on a specific piece of hardware or outside the scope of the library." Later releases have followed since.

purpose: Reading the operating system's random number generator for key generation, content-encryption keys, initialization vectors, PBES2 salts and ECDH-ES ephemeral keys.

audit.note: No public independent audit found. It is widely deployed.
